title: Creating elements
objective: Create new elements with createElement, draw a list from an array (render), remove elements and use dataset
story: It's building time on Planet DOM! So far you've changed elements that already existed on the page; today you'll make **new elements** from scratch with JavaScript and add them to the page.

sections.title: createElement and append
sections.body:
A new element is added in three steps: **create, fill, add**.

```js
const list = document.querySelector("#cargo");
const li = document.createElement("li"); // 1) create
li.textContent = "Oxygen tank";           // 2) fill
li.classList.add("item");
list.append(li);                           // 3) add to the page (at the end)
```

`createElement` only creates the element in memory; it isn't visible on the page until you add it somewhere. `append` adds at the end, `prepend` at the start. You can also put elements inside another element: `li.append(button)`.

sections.title: remove() and clearing
sections.body:
`el.remove()` deletes the element from the page. To empty a box completely, just set its content to empty text:

```js
document.querySelector("#old").remove(); // delete one element
list.textContent = "";                    // empty the list
```

sections.title: A list from an array: render()
dataset: data-* attributes
sections.body:
You can store your own information on an element in attributes starting with `data-`. In JavaScript you reach them with `dataset`:

```js
li.dataset.id = 7;          // in HTML: <li data-id="7">
console.log(li.dataset.id); // "7" (always text!)
```

Dashed names become camelCase: `data-max-speed` → `dataset.maxSpeed`.

It's very handy together with event delegation: `e.target.dataset.index` tells you which record the clicked button belongs to. The value is text, so turn it into a number with `Number(...)` if you need one.

tasks.title: First elements
tasks.prompt:
Add two elements to the `#cargo` list with code:

1. Create an `<li>` that says `Oxygen tank` and add it with `append`.
2. Create an `<li>` that says `Water tank` and add it **at the start** with `prepend`.
tasks.html: Cargo List

tasks.title: A list from an array
tasks.prompt:
Complete the `render()` function:

- it clears `#cargo`,
- creates and adds an `<li>` for every item in the `items` array,
- writes the number of items into `#count` like `3 items`.

Try adding a new item to the array and calling `render()` again.
tasks.html: Cargo List

tasks.title: ID tags
tasks.prompt:
Every item has an ID (`id`). `render()` should write the item's name into every `<li>` and store its ID with `li.dataset.id`.

Then add **one** `click` listener to `#cargo`: it writes the clicked `<li>`'s ID into `#count` like `Selected ID: 12`.
tasks.html: Cargo List
hints: The clicked li: e.target, its ID: e.target.dataset.id

challenge.title: Add and delete
challenge.prompt:
Make the cargo list fully work:

- `render()` puts a button with the class `del` that says `Delete` inside every `<li>`; the button's `dataset.index` is the item's position in the array.
- When `#add` is clicked, the text in the `#item-name` box (cleaned with `trim()`) is added to `items`, the box is cleared and the list is redrawn. Empty text isn't added.
- Add one listener to `#cargo`: when a `Delete` button is clicked, that item is removed from the array with `splice` and the list is redrawn.

project_task.title: Inventory on screen
project_task.prompt:
The inventory should show on the game panel. Complete the `renderInventory()` function:

- it clears the `#inventory` list,
- and creates and adds an `<li>` with the class `item` for every thing in the `inventory` array.

Click Start on the page to see the inventory. Try adding a new item to the inventory and calling `renderInventory()` again.
